title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb mince under a mashed potato crust
excerpt: Lamb mince cooked slowly with vegetables and stock until rich and saucy, topped with creamy mashed potato and baked until golden. A British winter staple.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie is a British dish, the name referring to the shepherd who tends sheep — hence the lamb filling, as opposed to cottage pie which uses beef. Both dishes are essentially the same preparation: minced meat cooked in gravy, topped with mashed potato and baked. The dish dates to the late 18th or early 19th century, when it emerged as a practical way of using leftover roast meat. The modern version uses raw mince rather than cooked meat. The distinction between shepherd's pie (lamb) and cottage pie (beef) is clear in British usage though often ignored elsewhere.

recipeTools.notes: For the filling and the mash.
A deep ovenproof dish or casserole, about 2 litres, that can go from hob to oven.

content.text: The filling needs to be cooked down until fairly dry before the mash goes on top: a wet filling will bubble up through the mash during baking. The mash should be beaten until very smooth and creamy, not stiff: a stiff mash is hard to spread evenly and does not brown as well. Forking the surface of the mash before baking creates ridges that catch and crisp. Let the pie rest for 10 minutes after taking it from the oven before serving.

items.preparation: floury, peeled and cut into chunks

content.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan over high heat. Brown the lamb mince in batches until coloured. Remove and set aside. In the same pan, cook the onion, carrot, and celery over medium heat for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Stir for 1 minute.

Return the lamb to the pan. Add the tomato puree and Worcestershire sauce. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the stock and simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes until the liquid has reduced and the filling is fairly dry. Add the peas in the last 2 minutes. Season. Transfer to a large baking dish.
Make the mash: boil the potatoes until tender. Drain and steam dry for 2 minutes. Pass through a ricer or mash until smooth. Beat in the butter and warm milk. Season well.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spread the mash over the filling, right to the edges. Fork the surface into ridges. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
